video_title: NBA Legends On The Art Of 1v1 Scoring, Elite Footwork & Basketball Fundamentals

quotes.speaker: Vince Carter
quotes.summary_phrase: Vince Carter on the importance of fundamental footwork in guarding elite scorers
quotes.excerpt: No one is going to beat me on fundamentals.
quotes.quote: All of you guys were so fundamentally sound. When trying to guard you, because you and Kobe and Mike, you three in terms of footwork, drove me crazy. It drove me crazy because I preached my game on being fundamentally sound. That's how I was taught from my dad, high school, college, fundamentals, fundamentals. No one is going to beat me on fundamentals. When I want to get you off, I think I have better footwork. That's what made you, and then some that you're 6'10".

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on the evolution of footwork and athleticism in modern NBA players
quotes.excerpt: They had footwork and athleticism. So you either had one or the other. Mike was different.
quotes.quote: They were younger coming in the league when you were already in the league. You were the guy. What did you see in them when they came in the league and being in your position? I didn't have athleticism, so they had footwork and athleticism. So you either had one or the other. Mike was different. He had them both. So you saw the evolution of our game. It was only Mike, and then Kobe and them. Then it was them with footwork. They could beat you with their footwork, they could beat you with their shoulder work, they could post up, they could shoot over you, and then they could dunk over you. They had it all.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on teaching Aliyah Edwards to create space without excessive dribbling
quotes.excerpt: You don't need a lot of dribbles. In this area you trying to play three max.
quotes.quote: I was just at Girls ABCD in Oakland, and one of the players, Aliyah Edwards, plays in the WNBA. She's cold. She wants to play more around the free throw line and in the mid-post. I was like, how is your footwork? She's like, that's what I want to work on this summer. I was like, man, so that team is moving to Houston, and I live in Houston. I was like, come to my house, I'm going to work with you on that. I was telling her, you don't need a lot of dribbles. In this area you trying to play three max. You just need to know how to create space, and that's what I was so good at. I learned how to create space, and then when that space is created, the ball has to go up.

quotes.quote: I'm going to tell you when it started, USA. When Blake was after practice working on footwork. It's clips of like us just messing around. I'm like teaching him a double step back. quotes.speaker: Vince Carter
quotes.summary_phrase: Vince Carter on the two essential skills for 1v1 scoring success
quotes.excerpt: You've got to be able to two things: be able to create your own shot and score.
quotes.quote: To me, you've got to be able to two things: be able to create your own shot within one, two, or three, three dribbles max, and you've got to be able to score with contact. Minimal or a lot, you got to be able to score with contact.

quotes.speaker: Chauncey Billups
quotes.summary_phrase: Chauncey Billups on his non-pattern approach to 1v1 defense
quotes.excerpt: I'm a non-pattern guy. I'm not going to do the same thing twice.
quotes.quote: I'm a non-pattern guy. I'm not going to do the same thing twice. So I'm a non-pattern guy. You know what I mean? Like so I'm going to go right, right, I pull off off one leg right. Like what? Then I'll go right, crossover left, hang dribble that. Right, crossover left, dude then step like I'm never going to do the same thing twice. So now I got you guessing. So as long as I got you guessing I'm good.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady on his mid-post 1v1 scoring strategy
quotes.excerpt: I'm going to jab step you, take a shot. Then I'm going to do it again.
quotes.quote: I'm going to jab step you, take a shot. Then I'm going to do it again, I'm going to come back, do it again, I'm going to jab step, see how you react to it, or I'm just going to go right, pump fake, right, off of that one dribble, see how you react to that. If you jump, boom, I'm going to hit you, foul. And then I'm going to come back and then I'm going to go the other way. I'm going to I'm going to have you guessing so you don't know. So now it's going left, right, all the way one dribble, pull up.
